question: A system program that translates and executes an instruction at the same time is called:
solution:
The correct answer is__** **__**Interpreter**

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

The question describes a system program that:

 
• 
 
Translates an instruction (converts high-level code to machine code).

 
 
• 
 
Executes it immediately (line by line).

 

This matches the definition of an Interpreter:

__
 
• 
 
Interpreters translate and execute code one instruction at a time.

 
 
• 
 
Examples: Python, JavaScript, and BASIC use interpreters.

 

Why Not Other Options?

 
• 
 
Assembler (Option 2):

 
 
• 
 
Converts assembly language to machine code (does not execute it).

 
 
• 
 
Works on whole programs, not line by line.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Compiler (Option 3):

 
 
• 
 
Translates the entire program at once (does not execute immediately).

 
 
• 
 
Produces an executable file (e.g., C, C++).

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Operating System (Option 4):

 
 
• 
 
Manages hardware and software resources but does not translate or execute programs directly

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• An **operating system (OS)** is a program that, after being initially loaded into the computer by a boot program, manages all of the other application programs in a computer.
 
• The application programs make use of the operating system by making requests for services through a defined application program interface.
 
• **A compiler translates the entire source code in a single run.** An interpreter translates the entire source code line by line. It consumes less time i.e., it is faster than an interpreter.
 
• It consumes much more time than the compiler i.e., it is slower than the compiler. It is more efficient.
